content.thinking: Since there's no real data or root cause here, I should write an honest postmortem that clearly marks metrics and root cause as unknown rather than inventing numbers—structuring it with root_cause, executive_summary, and optional assumptions fields while avoiding fabricated durations or error rates.

assumptions: The alert itself is assumed to be genuine; with no metrics retrieved, it could not be confirmed and a false or misfiring alert has not been excluded.
The absence of recent flag changes is taken from a single read of the flag provider's history and was not cross-checked against deploys, infrastructure changes, or dependency health.
The start of impact is assumed to be the moment the alert fired; no onset was measured, and the fault may have begun earlier.
The service is assumed to still be affected, because no metrics were available to show recovery - not because recovery was checked and ruled out.
The gap in metrics is itself unexplained; it is assumed to be a retrieval or data-availability problem rather than a symptom of the same fault, but that was not investigated.
input.executive_summary: An automated alert reported that one of our internal services was returning an elevated share of failed requests. The automated responder picked the incident up and began investigating within seconds, but the monitoring data it needed for the affected period came back empty, so it could not confirm what was wrong, how many requests or customers were affected, or how long the problem lasted. No configuration or feature-flag changes were found that would explain it. Because there was no evidence to act on, no fix or mitigation was applied and the incident was handed to on-call engineers to continue. At the point the automated handling ended, the service had not been observed to recover, so customer impact should be treated as ongoing and of unknown size until a human investigation establishes otherwise.
input.root_cause: Not determined. An alert for an elevated error rate fired on io-shop, but the investigation could not retrieve any per-minute metrics for the incident window and the flag provider showed no recent changes, so no candidate cause could be supported or ruled out; the incident was escalated to humans for insufficient evidence.
